record.title: SSD-LLaMA reports trillion-parameter MoE inference on a single RTX 5090
record.summary: The SSD-LLaMA preprint describes an SSD-to-RAM-to-VRAM expert-delivery system with a three-tier cache and CPU–GPU execution placement for MoE inference. On a stated consumer testbed with one RTX 5090, 16 GB host DRAM and a 4 TB NVMe SSD, the authors report running a 2.8T-parameter Kimi-K3 at 1.217 prefill tokens/s and 0.465 decode tokens/s. Section 5.4 reports baseline-specific throughput gains, while the abstract and conclusion give different aggregate ranges; the exact mapping is unresolved. These are paper-reported measurements, not an independent reproduction.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that SSD-LLaMA runs a 2.8T-parameter Kimi-K3 on a consumer testbed with one RTX 5090, 32 GB VRAM, 16 GB host DRAM and a 4 TB NVMe SSD, reaching 1.217 prefill tokens/s and 0.465 decode tokens/s.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For batch-size-1 tests across three evaluated MoE models, Section 5.4 reports prefill throughput gains of 1.90×–3.61× over llama.cpp and 1.06×–2.92× over KTransformers, and decode gains of 1.35×–3.44× over llama.cpp and 1.57×–15.61× over KTransformers; comparisons to Colibri are limited to GLM-5.2.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper's abstract and conclusion instead summarize prefill gains as 1.52×–4.19× and decode gains as 2.10×–15.58×. The source does not reconcile these aggregate ranges with the baseline-specific Section 5.4 values, so no single aggregate range is treated as settled here.

contradictory_evidence: Within this same paper, the abstract and conclusion report prefill 1.52×–4.19× and decode 2.10×–15.58×, while Section 5.4 reports different baseline-specific ranges (including 1.06×–3.61× prefill and 1.35×–15.61× decode across its named comparisons). The difference may reflect a different aggregation or comparison set, but the paper does not resolve it.

evidence_gaps.description: The Kimi-K3 rates and baseline comparisons have not been independently reproduced, and implementation/checkpoint correspondence has not been audited.
The abstract/conclusion aggregate speedup ranges differ from the baseline-specific ranges in Section 5.4; the comparison set and aggregation are not reconciled.

brief.importance_rationale: If reproduced, SSD-backed expert delivery could make a 2.8T MoE model locally runnable on one consumer GPU with modest host DRAM, changing the practical capacity/latency tradeoff. The paper reports only 0.465 decode tokens/s for Kimi-K3, and its aggregate speedup ranges conflict across sections; the result is notable but not a demonstrated consumer deployment frontier.
limitations: All performance results are author-reported and were not independently reproduced; the paper's executable artifact and exact checkpoint revisions were not inspected.
The paper reports a 0.465 tokens/s decode rate for 2.8T Kimi-K3; the abstract's greater-than-one-token-per-second phrase should not be read as a decode-rate result.
The abstract/conclusion prefill and decode ranges (1.52×–4.19× and 2.10×–15.58×) do not match the baseline-specific ranges reported in Section 5.4; the source does not explain the aggregate mapping.
The testbed is one configuration with batch size 1 and two prompt workloads; performance on other SSDs, CPUs, GPU memory configurations, concurrency levels and serving workloads is unknown.
The source's cost discussion is an estimate; this review did not verify hardware prices, energy, utilization, service cost or field deployment.
brief.summary: The SSD-LLaMA preprint describes an SSD-to-RAM-to-VRAM expert-delivery system with a three-tier cache and CPU–GPU execution placement for MoE inference. On a stated consumer testbed with one RTX 5090, 16 GB host DRAM and a 4 TB NVMe SSD, the authors report running a 2.8T-parameter Kimi-K3 at 1.217 prefill tokens/s and 0.465 decode tokens/s. Section 5.4 reports baseline-specific throughput gains, while the abstract and conclusion give different aggregate ranges; the exact mapping is unresolved. These are paper-reported measurements, not an independent reproduction.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that SSD-LLaMA runs selected MoE models on a single consumer RTX 5090 and outperforms named CPU/GPU and SSD-offload baselines in batch-size-1 tests. The specific 2.8T Kimi-K3 result is 1.217 prefill tokens/s and 0.465 decode tokens/s; aggregate speedup ranges conflict between the abstract/conclusion and Section 5.4.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper models hardware capacity costs and reports an SSD/DRAM capacity-tier advantage, but no independently verified purchase-cost, energy, utilization or total-cost-of-service result was established in this review.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper reports the stated hardware setup, Kimi-K3 rates and baseline comparisons. the research desk inspected the paper's current v1 HTML and fetched the PDF but did not independently reproduce the measurements, inspect runnable code or verify the cited model checkpoints.
technical.implementation_status: Preprint-described prototype and author-reported testbed measurements; no independently runnable implementation or reproduction was verified.
technical.mechanism: Stores the full expert pool on NVMe and stages selected experts through host RAM into VRAM. The paper combines fixed-offset expert packs, asynchronous SSD reads and transfers, a three-tier cache, lossless block compression, and CPU/GPU placement selected using end-to-end token latency.
technical.novelty: A coordinated SSD–RAM–VRAM expert-delivery pipeline for sparse MoE inference that combines direct expert-pack reads, overlap, caching and CPU/GPU placement rather than treating SSD capacity as ordinary memory mapping.
technical.regime: Author-reported MoE inference on an Intel Ultra5 230F, RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 16 GB host DRAM and 4 TB NVMe SSD rated up to 9 GiB/s sequential read/write. Baseline tests use batch size 1 on MMLU and Alpaca; the paper evaluates DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K2.7-Code and GLM-5.2, and separately reports Kimi-K3 throughput.
technical.reproducibility: Current arXiv v1 HTML and API metadata were inspected and the PDF fetched. No independent run was performed. The paper's reported aggregate prefill/decode speedup ranges conflict with its Section 5.4 baseline-specific ranges; exact comparison scope remains unresolved.
technical.strongest_baseline: Section 5.4 compares against llama.cpp and KTransformers across the three stated model families, and Colibri only on GLM-5.2. The paper reports baseline-specific gains but its abstract/conclusion aggregate ranges do not reconcile with those section values.

brief.title: SSD-LLaMA reports trillion-parameter MoE inference on a single RTX 5090
brief.why_it_matters: SSD-backed expert delivery may lower the hardware capacity needed to load large MoE models locally, which could change where inference is feasible. The reported Kimi-K3 decode rate is below one token per second, and the paper's speedup ranges conflict across sections, so it does not establish a general consumer-PC performance or cost frontier.
